I am Ahsan Mahmood, an AI-native full-stack developer in Lahore with 8+ years of hands-on experience. AI agents write most of my code now; I decide what they build, review it and confirm it works. That is one way to get software made. These are the other five, including the jobs where I would send you to them. Find my work: aoneahsan.com · the Android app on Google Play · every place my work is published

I can write all of this by hand, and for most of my career I did. I work through AI agents now because they produce code far faster than I can. I decide what gets built and how, I tell them, and I review what comes back. Nothing is finished until I have confirmed it is correct. What took me a month now takes a day or a week, and I would put the change at 10 to 100 times. That is my own statement from doing the work rather than a measurement, so read it beside the dates here.

None of these is the wrong answer. Each one fits some jobs better than I do, and its page says which. An agency — Choose it when the work needs several people at the same hour. An inexperienced developer — Choose it when the job is small and the mistakes are cheap. A vibe coder — Choose it when you want to test an idea on real people this week. A freelancer from a large marketplace — Choose it for a small job with a clear finish. Doing it in-house — Choose it when the software is the business and needs someone every day for years.
documents.s: Five other ways to get this built, and how I compare

documents.t: I am Ahsan Mahmood, a full-stack developer in Lahore. This guide sits beside my portfolio: the projects I can show, the work I take on, and the released products I have built with Zaions. I have more than eight years of hands-on development experience. I can write the code myself. Today I also direct AI agents, read what they produce and check the result against the product people will actually use. The difference matters at both ends of a build. Choosing what to make, setting boundaries and deciding whether the finished work is correct still take experience. An agent can move quickly through an implementation; it cannot take responsibility for the decision to ship it. That remains mine.

I want the working product to carry more weight than a claim about it. A client project I can show belongs here. So do my skills and the products that are live. Each release in the ecosystem has a direct destination; you can leave this guide and inspect it yourself. A private or unfinished project does not join that list because a polished description would tell you less than a working page. The comparison pages in this guide describe ways of getting software built. They do not compare other people's profiles. They explain the decisions a buyer will face when choosing an agency, a marketplace, an early-career developer or one person who can carry the work from scope to release. The answer depends on the job. The dates, prices and limits on the main site are there so you can decide with more than a slogan.

These dates describe this site, not a delivery promise for somebody else's project. 31 July 2026: Planning and the first design pages began. 16 August 2026: The rebuilt app received its first commit. 21 August 2026: The rebuild took over aoneahsan.com. 5 November 2026: The site moved to a new host. The design pages came before the rebuilt app. The live site then gave the work a harder test: pages had to render, links had to arrive at the right place, and the build had to keep serving after I stopped looking at it. The guide you are reading is part of the same record. It explains the work without requiring someone to sign in first.

I decide what gets built. Then I check it. Agents help me move through implementation, but the code, browser behaviour and handover still need review. A green build is one piece of evidence; it does not tell me whether a person can finish the task on a phone, whether a link leads to a live release, or whether an answer on a public page is true. If you have a project in mind, contact me through the portfolio. Tell me what it needs to do. I will look at the work and say where I fit. You can also browse the released Zaions products or visit Zaions to see the team around them.

A hiring route is easier to choose once you name who will own the decisions after the first release. A demo needs one kind of help. A product with accounts, data and a store listing needs another. I am Ahsan Mahmood. I build web and Android products, and I direct AI agents as part of that work. These notes are for deciding whether to call me at all. The fuller comparison on my site shows the shipped work behind each route.
documents.s: Choose a way to build your software — a route checklist

documents.t: Write down the smallest outcome you can check in a browser or on a device. Then answer these questions before choosing a supplier: Does the work need several people at once? If design, engineering and support must run in parallel under one contract, read the agency checklist. Can someone already on your team review the code? A newer developer can be the right hire for bounded work when a senior can make the technical calls. Use the newer-developer checklist. Are you still testing whether anyone wants the idea? A generated prototype can answer that without a production build. The AI-prototype checklist names what must be checked before you keep it. Is there one clear deliverable and a short finish line? A marketplace freelancer can be a sensible route, especially when escrow matters. Will the software need daily attention for years? Plan for your own team. An outside developer can build the first release, but should not become the only person who can run it. The routes can overlap. A founder may use a prototype to test the idea, hire an agency for a fixed date, then employ engineers to own the product. Decide who checks each handover; a change of supplier does not make an untested feature work.

My projects are the evidence for my side of this choice. Rent Party shows a product with rules, computer players and online rooms. The portfolio rebuild records the work behind this site. CallVault shows an Android app and web dashboard, with the limitation that it is not on Google Play. Those links let you inspect what shipped. They do not tell me the scope or date for your job. I would need to hear that first.
documents.s: What I can show before a call

documents.t: A short brief is enough to begin: what a user must be able to do, what already exists, which accounts and data are involved, and what deadline is real. Write to me if one developer owning the build and handover fits. The first call is free and lasts thirty minutes; I will say if another route fits better. Last checked 28 November 2026

An agency is a good choice when your deadline needs several specialists working at the same time. It can put design, development and support under one contract. The useful question is who will do each job after the proposal is signed.
documents.s: Agency hiring checklist for a software build

documents.t: A proposal can name a team without telling you who is allocated to your work. Ask for the roles, the expected time from each role and the person who can answer a technical question without routing it through an account manager. If a designer and developer need to settle a decision together, find out how that happens. An agency's bench can protect a schedule when someone leaves or falls ill. Ask how a replacement learns the code and who checks a handover. That is a fair reason to choose a team over one developer.
documents.s: Ask who will actually build it

documents.t: Give each agency the same brief. Ask each to name the first release, the work outside the quote, how changes are priced and what support begins after launch. A cheaper number with a smaller release is not the same offer. Clutch's 2026 software development pricing guide reports that projects reviewed on its directory typically cost $10,000–$49,999. That range describes its reviewed projects, not an agency quote for your brief. Clutch's pricing guide was checked on 28 November 2026; open the source before using the range in a budget.

Ask where the repository, domain and service accounts will live. Ask who can deploy a fix, who receives an error report, and what happens if the agency changes the people assigned to you. A handover is useful only if somebody outside the original team can follow it. I work as one developer directing AI agents, so I cannot promise several people at the same hour or a support rota. My full agency comparison explains that trade and links to Rent Party and the portfolio rebuild as work you can open. If you want one person to own the decisions from data model through release, send me the brief. If parallel staffing is the requirement, an agency is the clearer fit. Compare the other routes Last checked 28 November 2026

A marketplace is useful when one task has a clear end and you want payment held until you approve it. A bug fix, a single screen from an existing design or a landing page can fit. The brief should make acceptance visible to both sides.
documents.s: Choose a marketplace freelancer for a bounded job

documents.t: Show the current page or error, describe the exact change and say how you will test it. Name the files or account access you can provide. Ask bidders what they need before they begin. If a bid depends on assumptions about data or existing code, settle those assumptions before choosing the lowest figure. A profile rating records earlier buyers' experience with earlier jobs. Look for an example close to yours, then ask the bidder to explain one decision in that work. That tells you more than a star count alone.
documents.s: Make the job small enough to quote

documents.t: The platform can hold a payment and provide a dispute route. It does not inspect your code, run your release or maintain your service afterward. Put the review and handover in the agreed deliverable: repository access, a way to run the work and a short record of what changed. Freelancer.com lists an employer fee of 3% or $3, whichever is greater, when a fixed-price project is awarded; hourly projects carry 3% of each payment. The freelancer's own rate is separate. That is one platform's published fee. Its fees and charges page was checked on 28 November 2026.

I can show ClearHire and LifeWell as products rather than ask you to rely on a marketplace rating. My full comparison explains why I scope a product before giving a fixed number. A direct call and written scope take longer than selecting a bid. For one bounded change, that overhead may not earn its place. For a product whose build, data and release need one owner, send me the brief and I will tell you whether the scope fits. Compare the other routes Last checked 28 November 2026
documents.s: When to use a direct arrangement

documents.t: Build your own team when the software is central to the business and needs attention every day. An employee can stay close to the people using it, learn why decisions were made and keep that knowledge after a first release.
documents.s: Plan an in-house team for a product you will keep

documents.t: List what happens after launch: user support, feature requests, security fixes, provider changes and releases. If those jobs never stop, a one-off contract does not replace an internal owner. Name the person who will decide priorities and the person who can ship an urgent correction. Hiring takes time. While the team is forming, decide who maintains the existing service and who reviews the first engineer's work. A vacant senior role cannot be hidden inside a junior hire's job description.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports a May 2025 median wage of $135,980 a year for US software developers. Its lowest-paid tenth earned less than $82,460; its highest-paid tenth earned more than $214,670. These are wages, not a whole team's cost. Recruiting, benefits and equipment are additional. The BLS occupation page was checked on 28 November 2026. Use the figure to frame a US hiring conversation, not to decide a contractor's quote or a salary in another country.

An outside developer can help before the permanent team exists. Agree in advance where the repository, domain, database and release accounts will live. Require a build that a new engineer can run, a record of decisions and a release process the team can repeat. I can work on that stretch or on an existing codebase that needs an audit. LabFlow and this portfolio rebuild are open examples. My full in-house comparison explains the handover I expect. I am also open to remote roles when a business wants a senior engineer inside the team. If you need ongoing daily ownership, hire for it. If you need the first release while that team is being assembled, tell me what exists now. Compare the other routes Last checked 28 November 2026
documents.s: Put the first release in your own hands

documents.t: Hire a newer developer when the task has a small boundary and somebody experienced can review the result. A brochure site, an internal script or a prototype that you expect to replace can fit. The reviewer is part of the plan, even if that person is not writing the code.
documents.s: When to hire a newer developer

documents.t: Write the deliverable as a behavior you can try, rather than a technology list. Include the input, the expected output and one failure case. A task that keeps gaining accounts, payments or sensitive data has moved beyond the small job you first described. Set aside time for review before the release date. If there is no senior on your side, ask the developer who will decide the architecture and inspect the changes. Energy and a low rate do not create that missing role.
documents.s: Give the task a finish line

documents.t: Have the developer show the feature running with a real example. Check who owns the repository and how the next person will start the project. A written note about one awkward decision is more useful than a large document assembled after delivery. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics does not label an entry-level software developer wage. Its May 2025 figure says the lowest-paid tenth of US software developers earned less than $82,460 a year. That is an employee wage in the United States, not a freelance quote or a rate for every newer developer. The BLS occupation page was checked on 28 November 2026; read the source if you are using it for a hiring budget.
documents.s: Ask for evidence of the work

documents.t: I have shipped production software since January 2018. Video Controls Plus and LabFlow show different kinds of work that stayed in development well beyond a first commit. My full comparison explains what I check when AI agents write code and why I can take over a wrong turn by hand. For a bounded job with a reviewer already in place, that experience may be more than you need. For a product whose failures will be expensive to undo, tell me what you are building and who will own it after launch. Compare the other routes Last checked 28 November 2026
documents.s: Where my experience changes the choice

documents.t: Use an AI app builder when the question is whether people want the idea. A working screen can be enough to put in front of a few users this week. You do not need to commission a production system to learn whether they can complete the first task.
documents.s: Use an AI-generated prototype, then decide what to keep

documents.t: Pick one user action and watch someone try it. If they cannot find the action or do not value the result, change the idea before adding infrastructure. Save the prompt, the generated code and the feedback so the next build begins from what you learned. Do not use the first visual finish as a security review. When the prototype will hold real accounts, payments or private records, someone has to inspect authorization, error paths, quotas and deployment. The generated app cannot certify those conditions by saying it is ready.
documents.s: Decide what the prototype must prove

documents.t: Bolt lists Pro at $25 a month with monthly billing. Lovable lists Pro at $25 a month with 100 monthly credits. Replit publishes separate plans and allowances. Those are tool prices, not the cost of maintaining the resulting app. Sources checked on 28 November 2026: Bolt pricing, Lovable pricing and Replit pricing. Read the current limits before choosing one.
documents.s: Budget for the tool and the person checking it

documents.t: Decide whether to harden the prototype or rebuild from the findings. Ask whoever takes it on to show a non-admin sign-in, one forbidden data read, a failed network request and the route after a fresh load. Those checks expose a different class of problem from a screenshot. I use AI agents too. I decide what they build, read the code and run the result. The full comparison shows how defects slipped past automated checks during my portfolio rebuild, and CallVault is an Android and web example. If the idea has passed its first user test and now needs a release, send me the brief. If the idea is still untested, build the prototype first. Compare the other routes Last checked 28 November 2026

AChat makes the first contact a choice. I can point to its web and Android app, and to the three ways someone can find another person without exchanging a phone number. The question: How can people connect without sharing a phone number?

A username, invitation link or QR code gives a person a way to reach someone they chose. That is a narrower request than handing over a phone number. The product also has anonymous rooms that can be opened without an account.
documents.s: What changes at the first invitation?

documents.t: The released web app is the direct destination here. The roster also records an Android surface. I would check those actual entry points before describing a messaging experience as shipped.

The published facts describe discovery and anonymous rooms. They do not promise that every conversation is anonymous or that no information is ever stored. A useful portfolio page should keep that distinction visible.

A username, an invite link and a QR code all solve the first contact, but they ask different things of the people using them. The published release gives those choices alongside an anonymous room that does not need an account. I would inspect each entry point on the live web app, then check the Android surface recorded for the same product. The useful engineering question is whether a person can tell which kind of conversation they are entering before they share an address or start a room. The roster gives the routes into a chat. It does not settle every privacy question about the chat afterward.
documents.s: Why keep these ways of meeting separate?

documents.t: AChat is a messaging app on the web and Android for chosen people. People can find a user by username, invite link or QR code without a phone number. Anonymous rooms can be opened without an account.

CallVault keeps the phone library at the centre of the experience. A person can play, search, annotate and export recordings there; private cloud backup is something they choose to enable. The question: When does a call recording leave the phone?

The app records calls through the audio source a phone makes available. That qualification matters: Android devices and call routes differ, so the page should not promise a uniform capture result on every handset.
Playback, search and notes make a recording useful after the call. Export is an explicit action from the phone library rather than a reason to move every file to a server by default.
documents.s: How is a recording found later?

documents.t: The roster says recordings stay on the phone unless private cloud backup is enabled. I would check that choice in the app before describing its data flow more broadly.
documents.s: What stays under the user’s control?

documents.t: Backup does. The phone library already has playback, search, notes and export, so the recording can be useful without first moving it to a cloud account. Private cloud backup is a choice the person enables. That order is significant for an app handling call audio: a list of features is less useful than knowing where the file stays until somebody asks otherwise. I would inspect the backup control and an exported recording on the released Android app, then check the actual audio source on the device being used. The published product cannot make every handset supply the same source.

CallVault records calls on Android through the audio source a phone makes available. Its phone library supports playback, search, notes and export. Recordings stay on the phone unless the user enables private cloud backup.

Capacitor Auth Manager is a package I can inspect as code and on npm. Its current public contract offers one Google sign-in call for web, Android and iOS. The question: How much sign-in code should three app targets share?
documents.s: Capacitor Auth Manager — a released Zaions product

documents.t: The package spans a browser and two native app targets. That gives a product team one public entry point for Google sign-in while the platform behaviour remains inside the package.
documents.s: What does the package put behind one call?

documents.t: Firebase is not required as a dependency. That is a concrete integration boundary, not a promise about every application that might use the package.
Google is the only enabled provider in version 3.x. I would rather name the available path than imply a menu of providers that the release does not contain.

I would start with the public Google sign-in call and follow it on web, Android and iOS, rather than infer platform support from one successful browser demo. The release says Firebase is not required as a dependency and that Google is the only enabled provider in version 3.x. Those are useful, testable limits. A team adopting the package still has to configure its own application and inspect the returned session on each target. The package is responsible for a consistent entry point; the consuming product remains responsible for its sign-in experience, account rules and what happens after authentication succeeds.
documents.s: How would I judge this package?

documents.t: Capacitor Auth Manager offers one Google sign-in call for web, Android and iOS. It does not require Firebase as a dependency. Google is the only enabled provider in version 3.x.

ClearHire brings resume writing and work-history verification into one career workflow. Its structured profile is the starting record rather than a pile of separately edited copies. The question: What evidence can sit behind a resume?

The product has an ATS-friendly builder with structured profiles. Its career tools include bullet writing and ATS checks; the roster records 50 or more tools, not an outcome guarantee for a job search.
Verified-employment workflows attach a checkable process to a claim; an employer still judges it.
documents.s: What adds trust to work history?

documents.t: The released product is linked directly. A hiring manager can inspect its actual resume and profile flow before deciding what the claims mean in practice.

A candidate can begin with a structured profile, turn that record into an ATS-friendly resume and use tools such as bullet writing and ATS checks. The published count is more than fifty career tools, but that number says little about whether a particular resume states the right work. The verified-employment workflow is another inspectable step: it adds a way to check a claim without making the hiring decision for an employer. I would follow one profile through its resume output and then inspect what a verification actually shows. The product can make evidence easier to present. It cannot promise a job offer.
Build a sharper resume and get discovered. ATS-friendly resume builder with structured profiles 50+ career tools — from bullet writing to ATS checks Verified-employment workflows that add trust

Eat This starts with the way a person is choosing food: a nutrient, a feeling or a time of day. The result is grounded in a serving rather than an unexplained recommendation. The question: What does one serving actually provide?
documents.s: Eat This — a released Zaions product

documents.t: Someone can search by nutrient, feeling or time of day. That makes three distinct ways into the same food choice, without requiring the person to know a food name first.
The app shows how much of a nutrient one serving gives and identifies a cheap pick. A serving is the unit that lets a person compare a result with what they might actually eat.
Food search flags when a question belongs with a doctor; it does not give medical advice.

The serving size makes it comparable. A nutrient amount without a serving leaves the reader guessing what the number refers to; this app ties the contribution to one serving and can point to a cheap pick. The search itself starts from a nutrient, a feeling or the time of day, which are three ordinary ways a person might arrive without a food name. I would inspect a result reached from each route and read the quantity it shows. When the question belongs with a doctor, the product says so. That boundary matters more than adding a confident sentence the food data cannot support.
documents.s: What makes a food result usable?

documents.t: Eat This lets a person look for food by nutrient, feeling or time of day. It shows how much of a nutrient one serving gives. It identifies a cheap pick and when a question belongs with a doctor.
Visit Eat This Read Eat This documentation See all released Zaions products

Empora groups WooCommerce modules in one WordPress plugin. The useful choice is at the merchant’s end: which modules to switch on for that store. The question: Can a store install one plugin without adopting every module?
The released product puts store modules in one plugin. The roster does not enumerate each module here, so I would send a merchant to the live product for its current list.
A web dashboard handles licences and optional store connections. That makes the plugin and the management surface two parts of the same released workflow.
Modules can be switched on selectively. That is a more useful description than assuming every WooCommerce store wants the same set of additions.
documents.s: Which decision stays with the merchant?

documents.t: With the merchant. Empora packages WooCommerce modules together, but it lets a store switch on the modules it needs rather than treating the whole catalogue as one mandatory installation. The web dashboard has a separate job: it manages licences and optional store connections. I would inspect those two surfaces together, because an enabled module and a configured connection are different facts. The public roster does not list every module or promise that a particular store setup is supported. A merchant should open the current product list and check the exact module before planning a rollout around it.
documents.s: Where does the choice of scope live?

documents.t: Empora puts WooCommerce store modules in one WordPress plugin. A merchant chooses which modules to switch on. Its web dashboard handles licences and optional store connections.

HabitForge makes consistency visible as a rope. The mark changes with check-ins and also shows where a person stopped, which is more honest than showing only a successful count. The question: What does a habit history show when a streak breaks?
The rope thickens with each check-in and frays at a gap. The shape communicates a history that a single streak number would flatten.
The roster records friends, challenges and a leaderboard that a person can leave. Those are options around the personal record, not a condition for keeping it.
The current web and Android apps can be inspected directly.

A thickening rope records that check-ins happened; a frayed place records a pause. Both are part of the same history. The social pieces in the release — friends, challenges and a leaderboard — surround that personal record, and the leaderboard can be left. I would inspect a run of check-ins with a gap, then check whether the visual still tells the truth without a contest attached. The web and Android surfaces are both recorded for one account. The portfolio can describe the visible metaphor and the released platforms. It should not turn a habit tool into a promise that somebody will keep a streak.
Turns consistency into a rope you can see. A rope that thickens with every check-in and frays where you stopped Friends, challenges and a leaderboard you can leave Web and Android, from one account
Visit HabitForge Read HabitForge documentation See all released Zaions products

LabFlow joins patients, orders, samples and results in one laboratory system. Its meaningful boundary is the validation step between a draft result and a released one. The question: When is a lab result ready to leave the workflow?
Patient and order records sit alongside samples and results. Billing, inventory and quality control are part of the published product too, so the result does not live in an isolated form.
The roster names a validation workflow from draft to released. That is the step I would inspect when assessing whether the software respects the way a laboratory works.
It describes the product workflow, not clinical accuracy or a regulatory certification. Those would need their own evidence and are not supplied by a portfolio link.

Between a draft result and a released one. LabFlow keeps patient records, orders, samples and results in one system, but keeping them together is only the starting point. The validation workflow is the point at which a result changes status and becomes ready for its next reader. Billing, inventory and quality control are part of the same published product, so I would also inspect how those records sit beside an order. The release record establishes that the steps exist. The dry run is a preview, not permission to delete personal files. A cleanup product is credible when the exact path and consequence are visible before a click.

After a real run, a receipt records what happened. I would inspect a dry run before choosing any removal, then compare its promised paths with the receipt rather than relying on a broad word such as cleanup. NetCage controls network access for selected Android apps. A rule can target Wi-Fi, mobile data or both; the rest of the phone can stay connected. The question: Can one app go offline without disconnecting the phone?
The selected app and connection type are the decision. That is narrower than switching off Wi-Fi or mobile data for the whole device.
Profiles group apps and apply rules on chosen days and times. The roster establishes the scheduling capability, while the live product shows how those choices are made.
A rule should make its target and effect clear before it changes connectivity.

A network rule can block Wi-Fi, mobile data or both for one selected Android app while other apps remain online. If the target is unclear, a person can mistake a per-app rule for a device-wide switch. Profiles add another layer: groups of apps can receive rules on chosen days and times. I would inspect both the immediate rule and its scheduled version, including how the app shows which connection type is affected. The roster establishes the available controls. The live Android product is where a visitor can check the confirmation and status the software actually gives before depending on a rule.
documents.s: Why does the target need to be explicit?

Players can pass one phone around, play against CPU characters or open an online room. Those are distinct ways to gather a table without changing the underlying game.
The product handles the bank and keeps deeds in place on resume. That continuity is the reason a paused match can remain a match rather than becoming a new setup.

The bank and deeds remain in place when the game resumes. That matters for all three recorded ways to play: passing one phone around, sitting opposite CPU characters or opening an online room. Without the state of the bank and ownership, a paused match would become a fresh setup wearing the old name. I would inspect the transition out of a game and back into it, then check whether each mode presents the same essential state. The release record describes the available modes and continuity. It does not claim a particular rules variant or an outcome for every match.

documents.t: At the registered Android device, not at the moment a web page says a job was queued. Chosen stops can stay in place while other stops are ordered around them. That lets a driver protect a commitment without freezing every part of the day.
The chosen route remains visible beside an option to return or take a new route. A wrong turn does not silently erase the plan the driver made.
It is a planning layer over Google Maps, not a replacement for it.

The chosen route remains visible. Waylock lets a driver or courier hold selected stops in place while ordering the rest around them, then presents a choice to return to the old route or take a new one after a detour. I would inspect how those fixed stops are shown before departure and how the alternative appears when the road changes. The product is a planning layer over Google Maps, which is an important limit: it does not replace the underlying map service. Its value is in preserving a driver's decision while still allowing a new decision when the route changes.
